packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-97 — getClient() now performs an unconditional eager refresh_token POST + `prisma.credential.update` on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, ungated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, changing existing users' refresh semantics from jsforce lazy refresh to a mandatory network call whose failure (`response.statusText !== "OK"`, which is empty under HTTP/2) now throws and breaks the integration for non-sync users; the refreshed access_token is not even used by the returned Connection (P1, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:265 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` now throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" on schema mismatch for all users, whereas the removed code logged the zod error and continued with existing credentials; error behavior for existing non-sync Outlook users changed from tolerant to fatal without stated intent (P2, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` placeholder is injected in the non-sync branch too; in office365calendar the result is spread over o365AuthCredentials, so any provider response lacking refresh_token overwrites the real stored refresh token with the literal string "refresh_token" for non-sync users (P1, confidence 50)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — getClient now performs an unconditional Salesforce refresh_token round-trip plus `prisma.credential.update` on every client construction (not gated by expiry, not routed through refreshOAuthTokens), a behavior change to the existing Salesforce flow that is not traceable to the credential-sync requirement (P1, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:90 — Salesforce bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` entirely and always calls login.salesforce.com, so the stated "credential sync" intent is under-scoped for this app while every other touched app is routed through the sync endpoint (P2, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` replaces `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` with a SafeParseReturn wrapper (`{success, data}`) that is then persisted as the credential key, altering the existing non-sync Google refresh flow as a side effect of the refactor (P1, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262 — the refactor deletes the existing soft-fail path (`if (!tokenResponse.success) console.error(...)`) and, via parseRefreshTokenResponse, converts a tolerated schema mismatch into a thrown `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` even when credential sharing is disabled; this changes the pre-existing Outlook flow beyond what sync requires (P2, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` injects a placeholder refresh token into every parsed response for all apps regardless of whether sync is enabled, mutating the stored key shape of existing (non-sync) integrations (P2, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `WEBAPP_URL + \`/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback\`` replaces the `appConfig.slug`-derived redirect URI with a hard-coded literal; unrelated to OAuth credential sync and not traceable to any requirement (P3, confidence 100)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:1 — `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is imported from `@calcom/lib/constants` (also in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:3 and app-credential.ts:5) but no change to packages/lib/constants.ts is part of the diff, so the feature flag the whole change hinges on is under-scoped/undefined in this artifact (P1, confidence 50)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/add.ts:7 — the change moves encodeOAuthState/decodeOAuthState/createOAuthAppCredential to `_utils/oauth/` and rewrites 14 importers, but the diff contains no deletion of the original `_utils/{encodeOAuthState,decodeOAuthState,createOAuthAppCredential}.ts`, leaving a duplicate-module migration only half done (P2, confidence 50)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-26 — `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is a non-constant-time string compare on the only auth gate for an endpoint that writes credentials for any user, enabling byte-by-byte timing recovery of the webhook secret (P2, confidence 75)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-26 — handler never checks locally that CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is non-empty; if APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (defined outside this repo, unverifiable) is ever true without the secret set, an absent header yields `undefined !== undefined` === false and the auth check passes for everyone (P1, confidence 50)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16-30 — no `req.method` check, so GET/HEAD/PUT reach the secret gate and (with req.body undefined) hit `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` at :30 which throws an unhandled ZodError -> 500 with error detail/stack leaked in non-production, instead of 405/400 (P2, confidence 75)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:56-58 — `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` is unvalidated: any decryptable JSON (arrays, strings, huge objects, bogus token shapes) is written verbatim into `credential.key` for the caller-chosen `userId` at :71-90, so one leaked webhook secret + key gives full credential overwrite/planting for every user in the instance, and a missing/short key makes createDecipheriv throw an unhandled 500 (P2, confidence 50)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` sends no authentication (no secret header, no signature) and does not require https, so the external sync endpoint must hand out live OAuth access tokens to any unauthenticated caller who knows a numeric userId, and the tokens can transit in cleartext (P1, confidence 75)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:31-56 — for a `state.teamId` decoded from the attacker-controlled `?state=` query (decodeOAuthState.ts:9 does a bare JSON.parse with no schema), the only check is `members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }` (any plain member), and `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` at :59 is only reached on the non-team path with `teamId: null`, so any non-admin team member can create team-scoped app credentials for any team they belong to (P2, confidence 75)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:33-37 — webhook responds 404 "User not found" vs 200 for valid ids, letting a secret-holder (or, given the timing issue above, an attacker) enumerate valid Cal.com user ids; minor but compounding (P3, confidence 50)
none — no findings above threshold

gold_ce_only: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
gold_mrv_only: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

ce_bugs.t: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (including a guest just added by another guest) can add an unbounded number of arbitrary emails to a booking, turning the endpoint into an email-spam relay with no guest cap or rate limit.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No check on booking.status or endTime, so guests (and confirmation-style ICS emails) can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Attendees are committed to the DB before the calendar update and emails, and the email failure is swallowed with console.log, so the UI reports success while calendar/notifications may not have happened and a retry is rejected as duplicate.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Nothing prevents adding the organizer's own email (or the caller's own email) as an attendee, producing a booking where the host is also a guest.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not, so mixed-case emails (e.g. Foo@Blocked.com) bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS; existing-attendee check is also case-sensitive so duplicate attendees can be created.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:89 — Attendees are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees runs and that call is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar failure throws to the client after a partial (non-transactional) DB update with no rollback.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No check on booking.status/endTime, so guests can be added (and confirmation emails sent) for cancelled, rejected or past bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166 — sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, so a pre-existing attendee listed in input receives the "scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" email.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — message` is always a non-empty string (template literal), so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never fires and users see "undefined: ..." when err.data is missing.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` (admin AND owner), so the name contradicts the logic.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var is parsed inline in the handler rather than via a shared constant/config, and the guest emails are not lowercased before comparison so the lowercase map is inconsistent.
apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:44 — message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead fallback since the template literal is always truthy.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited with no try/catch after the attendees were already persisted, so a calendar/video provider error fails the request with the DB already mutated (client shows error, no emails sent, calendar out of sync, retry hits "emails_must_be_unique_valid").

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:103 — Attendee insert, calendar update, and email send are three non-atomic steps with no transaction or compensation; a failure at any later step leaves guests added in DB but never notified/synced.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:526 — sendAddGuestsEmails` emails every existing attendee and all team members on every add, but the handler passes `guests` (unfiltered input) rather than `uniqueGuests`; pre-existing attendees re-submitted get an AttendeeScheduledEmail duplicate "new booking" instead of the guests-added notice.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — Toast message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never fires and users see raw strings like "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR: undefined" or untranslated Prisma/calendar error text.
apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:38 — utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` is not awaited/caught inside `onSuccess`, so a refetch rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Blacklist and duplicate filtering compare case-sensitively (`guest === attendee.email`, `includes(guest)` against lowercased list), so mixed-case input bypasses both checks and creates duplicate attendee rows.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests` array has no max length and is not deduplicated server-side, so any authed user can trigger unbounded attendee inserts and unsolicited emails (sent under the organizer's name with .ics attachments) to arbitrary addresses.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming `guest` is not, so the blacklist is bypassed with mixed-case emails (e.g. Foo@Bar.com).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` should be `||`; as written team admins are denied and the check is effectively owner-only, diverging from the permission model used by sibling handlers (editLocation).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Authorization granted solely by matching the session email against unverified, booker-supplied attendee emails (case-sensitive compare, no verified/booking-status check) lets any attendee mutate the organizer's booking, push calendar updates via the organizer's event and mass-email all attendees.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Existing-attendee dedup uses case-sensitive `===`, allowing the same email to be re-added with different casing and re-spammed with invites.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — NOT_FOUND is returned before the authorization check while FORBIDDEN is returned after, letting any authed user enumerate which booking IDs exist.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Permission check requires isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner (should be OR) and no permission-matrix test (owner-only admin, attendee, unrelated user, teamId 0 fallback) exists to catch it.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Blacklist and duplicate filtering are case-sensitive (guest not lowercased, attendee email compared with ===) with no tests for mixed-case, partial-duplicate, or all-filtered input paths.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166 — updateCalendarAttendees is awaited unguarded after DB write, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but no email sent; no test covers this failure ordering or the swallowed sendAddGuestsEmails error.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — sendAddGuestsEmails fan-out (organizer, team members, new guests get scheduled email vs existing attendees get add-guests email) is untested; it is passed raw guests rather than uniqueGuests so filtered emails are misclassified.

mrv_bugs: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — booking is loaded with no status/time guard, so guests can be appended to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings and receive a "Guests Added"/CONFIRMED REQUEST invite for a meeting that will not happen (`const booking = await prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ...` with no `status`/`endTime` filter or post-load check; confidence 100; severity P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — duplicate detection is an in-memory check-then-insert with no UNIQUE(bookingId,email) invariant on Attendee, so two concurrent requests (or a double-click on the dialog's Add button) insert the same guest twice and each fires a separate email/calendar update (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` followed later by `createMany`; no transaction; confidence 75; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — nothing prevents the organizer's own email (or the acting user's) from being added as a guest, producing an attendee that is also the organizer and a self-addressed invite (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some(...) && !blacklisted...)` never checks `organizer.email`/`booking.userPrimaryEmail`; confidence 100; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:53 — ownership boundary is transitive: any attendee (including a guest just added by another guest) may add further guests, so the organizer loses control of the invite list and the attendee set can grow unboundedly without organizer involvement (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email); if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw`; confidence 75; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:160 — cascading failure with no compensation: attendees are committed at line 96, then `updateCalendarAttendees` can throw (external calendar/video API) and propagate a 500 to the UI after the DB write, leaving new attendees persisted but no calendar update and no emails sent, while the dialog reports failure (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` unguarded, followed by `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log(...) }` which silently drops email failures with no retry or error surfacing; confidence 100; severity P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests` is an unbounded array, so a single request can materialize thousands of Attendee rows, thousands of `getTranslation` awaits, and thousands of emails plus one calendar payload (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`; confidence 100; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58 — redundant, drift-prone second query: organizer is re-fetched by `booking.userId || 0` even though `user` was already `include`d on the booking, and `findFirstOrThrow` turns a user-less booking into an opaque 500 rather than a domain error (`const organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ...`; confidence 75; severity P3)

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531 — dead/unsatisfiable branch: the handler never populates `evt.team`, so team hosts/collective members are never notified and the per-member loop is a stand-in guard that always evaluates false (`if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { for (const teamMember of calendarEvent.team.members)`; confidence 75; severity P3)

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:31 — organizer subject is keyed off `attendees[0].name`, which for guest-added bookings can be the empty-string name assigned to new guests, yielding "Guests Added: X with  at ..." (`name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` while handler sets `name: ""` for guests; confidence 50; severity P3)

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 — new form primitive imports from the package root barrel (`@calcom/ui`) that in turn re-exports `MultiEmailLazy` -> `MultiEmail`, creating an intra-package circular import through `packages/ui/index.tsx` (`import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";` plus `export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy";`; confidence 50; severity P3)

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:26 — list rows are keyed by index while rows are removed by `splice(index,1)`, so React reuses DOM/input state across shifted entries and the removed row's focus/validation state lands on the wrong email (`<li key={index}>` with `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`; confidence 75; severity P3)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — no check of booking.status or endTime, so guests can be added (and calendar/emails fired) to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or past bookings (`const booking = await prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId, }`; confidence 100; severity P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:145 — seated events are not handled: attendees are createMany'd with no BookingSeat rows, no seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check, and seatsShowAttendees leaks the full list into every attendee's email (`seatsPerTimeSlot: booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot,`; confidence 75; severity P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — dedupe is case-sensitive against existing attendees and blacklist is lowercased but guest is not, so Foo@x.com bypasses both duplicate and blacklist filtering and creates a second attendee row (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`; confidence 100; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — emails are sent for the raw input `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`, so a submitted email that was already an attendee is treated as "new" and receives the AttendeeScheduledEmail (fresh confirmation) instead of the add-guests notice (`await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`; confidence 100; severity P2)

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:56 — isInvalidEmail is set true on failure but never reset when the user edits the emails or on successful submit/dialog close via overlay, so the error banner persists across reopen (`setIsInvalidEmail(true);`; confidence 100; severity P3)

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 — early return on empty array gives no feedback and leaves the dialog with no input rows (MultiEmail collapses to a button) so the primary Add button is a silent no-op (`if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }`; confidence 75; severity P3)

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — error toast prefixes the tRPC code and translates the raw message, so a server message like "you_do_not_have_permission" that has no translation is shown as-is, and the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead because the template string is never empty (`const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`; confidence 75; severity P3)

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 — subject uses attendees[0].name which is blank for guests and throws if attendees is empty; no guard (`name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name,`; confidence 75; severity P3)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — schema has no min(1) or max length on guests, so an empty array is accepted (then 400s with a misleading "emails_must_be_unique_valid") and there is no upper bound on attendees added per call (`guests: z.array(z.string().email()),`; confidence 100; severity P3)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:103 — attendee rows are committed via a standalone `prisma.booking.update({... attendees: { createMany ...}})` with no transaction around the subsequent unguarded `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (line 165), so a calendar/API failure leaves DB attendees persisted while the external calendar event and the client-facing error say nothing was added; there is no rollback or retry, and a user retry then hits `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the rows already exist (`await prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { attendees: true }, data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails } } } })`; confidence 75; severity P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — dedupe against existing attendees is a case-sensitive exact compare and the input email is never normalized to lowercase before insert (while the blacklist path lowercases), so `Alice@x.com` is inserted alongside existing `alice@x.com`, producing duplicate attendee rows for the same person on one booking (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`; confidence 75; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:56 — bookings whose owning user was deleted/nullified (`Booking.userId` is nullable in schema) hit `findFirstOrThrow` on `id: 0`, surfacing an unhandled Prisma NotFoundError as a 500 instead of a controlled TRPC error, and attendees are not added (`where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }` with `findFirstOrThrow`; confidence 75; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — the handler depends on `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` and `getUsersCredentials`, neither of which is present in this review-base (packages/core and packages/lib are absent from the diff and repo), so the write path to external calendar references cannot be verified and, if the method does not exist in the base, the mutation throws after the attendee rows have already been committed (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`; confidence 50; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — team permission check ANDs `isTeamAdmin` with `isTeamOwner` (owner is not admin in cal.com's MembershipRole checks; `isTeamAdmin` matches ADMIN||OWNER via `isTeamAdmin`'s own query only if implemented that way), so with `&&` the check can never be broader than plain owner and, when a team admin is the caller, the guard falls through to FORBIDDEN even though the dropdown action is shown to them (`(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`; confidence 75; severity P2)

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:540 — Function is named/intended to notify about added guests, but new guests receive the generic scheduled-booking email whose subject/body claim a fresh booking was made rather than that they were added to an existing one (`return sendEmail(() => new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee));`; confidence 75; severity P2)

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539 — Existing-attendee/organizer emails are decided from the raw `guests` input, but the handler only persists the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so a guest that was silently dropped (duplicate/blacklisted) is still treated as "new" by the email path and the UI toast "Guests added" reports success for guests that were not added (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` / `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`; confidence 75; severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:82 — Error message key "emails_must_be_unique_valid" ("Emails must be unique and valid") is thrown when all guests were already attendees or blacklisted, which tells the user their input was malformed rather than what actually happened (`throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" });`; confidence 75; severity P2)

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41 — onError builds a message that is always truthy (`"undefined: ..."` at worst), so the fallback toast "unable_to_add_guests" can never be shown and the declared fallback behavior does not happen (`const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`; showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error");`; confidence 100; severity P3)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:68 — handler introduces a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env-var filter into the add-guests flow that is not part of the requirement and silently drops emails without informing the caller (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`; confidence 50; severity P3)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no max length and no per-user rate limit, so an authenticated caller can push thousands of arbitrary addresses per call and the platform sends each a CONFIRMED ICS invite (spam/abuse vector, also amplifies calendar API calls in updateCalendarAttendees) (`guests: z.array(z.string().email()),`; confidence 100; severity P1)

ce_bugs.t: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — embed_category` is deleted unconditionally, but rows are only inserted when `embeddable_hosts` was non-blank; a site that used feed polling (`Jobs::PollFeed` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `import`) with an `embed_category` but no `embeddable_hosts` loses its category mapping entirely and silently begins filing every imported topic under a nil category, because `TopicEmbed.import` now derives the category solely from a matching `embeddable_hosts` row.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The TLD pattern `[a-z]{2,5}` rejects `.technology`/`.software`-class TLDs, punycode labels containing digits (`xn--p1ai`), `localhost`, and bare IPs, so those sites cannot be added through the UI; worse, the migration bypasses validation entirely, so such rows can exist in the DB and then fail to save the moment an admin edits them.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The INSERT is built by string interpolation of an admin-controlled site-setting value, so a single quote anywhere in the old `embeddable_hosts` setting aborts the migration mid-deploy (after the table was already created with `force: true`) and is a straightforward SQL injection sink.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — update` ignores the request body completely and re-renders the current state with 200 OK — a PUT that reports success while persisting nothing; `saveChanges` in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls it via `embedding.update({})` yet no template wires a button to that action, so the endpoint ships as a dead, silently-lying write API.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — category: eh.try(:category_id)` is nil whenever the imported URL's host has no `embeddable_hosts` row (notably RSS/feed-polling imports, which are not host-gated), so those topics now land in uncategorized where `SiteSetting.embed_category` used to apply globally

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The host value is string-interpolated straight into SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no quoting: a single apostrophe in the stored setting text breaks the statement and aborts the migration, and since the value is admin-supplied free text this is SQL injection executing as the database owner — use `quote(h)`/a bind parameter.

ce_bugs.t: packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — For a destination calendar row with a null credentialId the fan-out calls createEvent without an externalId while GoogleCalendarService resolves the target by credentialId match, so the event lands in "primary" and the reference records externalCalendarId undefined - a write that "succeeds" into the wrong calendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Credentials are fetched by raw id from the DB with no ownership or app-enabled check, bypassing getApps validation used in the constructor, so a destination calendar pointing at another user's or a globally disabled app's credential is still used to write events.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — On merge (newBookingId) only the first old calendar reference is deleted via `.find`, so the other hosts' old calendar events are orphaned after reschedule-into-existing-booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1067 — BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED payloads emit `destinationCalendar: null` while cancel/reject/payment paths now emit `[]`, so the same public field is inconsistently null vs empty array across triggers.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking whose destinationCalendar is null/[] throws a TypeError

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops all COLLECTIVE host calendars when the event type and organizer have no destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — createEvent matches destination calendars by credentialId, so legacy destination calendars with a null credentialId no longer match and the event is silently created on "primary" instead of the configured calendar

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — fallback `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is tautologically unreachable (it only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy), so calendarId becomes undefined instead of the destination calendar id

packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — credential` is declared once outside the per-reference loop, so if a reference's credential lookup fails the stale credential from the previous iteration is used to update that calendar

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — createEvent still always uses destinationCalendar[0], so with multiple destinations every host's event is written against the first host's calendar id (same issue at larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:452 — recurring cancellation still picks only the first `_calendar` reference per updated booking, so the extra host calendar events created by this feature are left behind
packages/core/EventManager.ts:598 — when the error is thrown before calendarReference is assigned the catch now returns an empty array instead of a failed EventResult, hiding the failure from callers
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:757 — the new loadUsers catch rewrites every error to 400/500, so an HttpError thrown inside loses its original status code and message context

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same dead branch as updateEvent — the `find` on `externalCalendarId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always yields undefined and silently falls back to "primary".

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-cancel block was moved inside the new per-reference loop but does not use `reference`, so the credentials x updatedBookings deleteEvent fan-out is repeated once per calendar reference (N x C x B redundant external deletes)

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:126 — CalDAV `createEvent` is now invoked once per destination but always resolves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (index 0), so each extra host adds a redundant `listCalendars()` DAV round-trip plus a duplicate write to the same calendar

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Office365 `createEvent` ignores the new `credentialId` argument and always targets the first destination's externalId, so N-1 of the N per-host calls are wasted duplicate writes to the same calendar

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — Destinations without a `credentialId` fan out to every credential of that integration type once per destination, so multiple such destinations multiply calendar API inserts

packages/core/EventManager.ts:369 — When no credential is found in memory or in the DB for a destination calendar, the host is silently skipped with no log and no failure EventResult, so the booking reports success while that host's calendar was never written.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Video booking references no longer persist `credentialId` (was `result.credentialId`), so handleCancelBooking.ts:491 skips deleteMeeting and cancelled bookings leave their video room live and joinable.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Credential is loaded by raw id from the DB with no userId/teamId or host-membership check, so any credentialId reachable via a DestinationCalendar row is used to write calendar events, bypassing the previous `this.calendarCredentials` ownership scoping.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — Same unscoped `prisma.credential.findUnique` fallback on the update path: a BookingReference.credentialId now drives use of an arbitrary user's calendar credential without an ownership check.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — No test covers destinationCalendar being an empty array, yet `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining and six call sites now emit `[]` (e.g. confirm.handler.ts:175, webhook.ts:119).

[]; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` dereferences `.integration` on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` with no optional chaining, so any booking whose `destinationCalendar` array is empty (the documented "no calendar" sentinel used everywhere else in this diff) and whose location is Google Meet throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to Cal Video — the exact "no Google Cal" case this line exists to handle is the case that crashes it; confidence 100, severity P0.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a silent no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (the exact sentinel set two lines earlier when the organizer/eventType has no destination calendar), so a COLLECTIVE booking where team members do have personal destination calendars but the organizer does not will silently drop all of those hosts' calendars — the specific "collective multiple host" scenario this task claims to fix; confidence 90, severity P0.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` dereferences the destructured element without a `?.`, so any Google Meet booking whose `destinationCalendar` is null/undefined/`[]` (handleNewBooking:1063 returns `null`, every other builder returns `[]`) throws TypeError and the booking 500s (conf 100, P0).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar), so the task's core case — collective hosts' calendars — is dropped with no warning (conf 90, P1).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — `minimumTokenResponseSchema`'s computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both stringify to the same literal (`"[object Object]"`), so the second overwrites the first. The "any numeric property is the expiry" and "allow other properties" behavior the comments promise does not exist; the schema is effectively `{access_token: string}` and, being a default stripping `z.object`, **discards every other field** (`refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, `scope`). In sync mode the stripped object is persisted, destroying the credential while reporting success — a textbook silent-pass gate. Needs `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — The sync `fetch` has **no timeout/abort signal**, no `response.ok` check, and no retry. Node fetch has no default timeout, so a hanging self-hosted endpoint blocks token refresh on the booking/availability hot path indefinitely, for every user of every OAuth app. A 4xx/5xx or HTML error page is returned as if it were a token response.

gold_mrv_only: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

ce_bugs.t: - `app/models/post.rb:130-137` — when `cook_method == raw_html`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`).
- `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16` — `<%= raw post.cooked %>` renders that unsanitized content directly, without escaping, to any anonymous visitor of `/embed/best`.

- `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36-39` — RSS feed item content (`i.content`) is unescaped via `CGI.unescapeHTML` and handed straight to `TopicEmbed.import` with **no tag/attribute allowlist at all** (unlike `import_remote`, which at least constrains Readability's output to a tag/attribute list). Any `<script>` in a polled feed item becomes a stored, rendered payload.

- `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` interpolates `url` into an HTML attribute/text **without escaping**. `url` is attacker-influenced: `EmbedController#best` accepts `embed_url` from a public request param, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the *host* component (`URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) — the path/query string is fully attacker-controlled. An unauthenticated request such as `GET /embed/best?embed_url=http:///x?y='>` will pass host validation, get queued via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` → `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and the raw `embed_url` string is spliced unescaped into the post body that is then persisted and rendered `raw` to every visitor of that embed.

- `app/models/topic_embed.rb:29` (`open(url).read`) — the host must match `embeddable_host`, but path/query is attacker-controlled, and `open-uri` follows redirects by default; a malicious or compromised target page could redirect the server to internal/other resources (SSRF surface). Given this era's `open-uri`, this is worth hardening rather than assuming it's safe.

gold_ce_only: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
gold_mrv_only: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting is empty (default ''), because the SQL JOIN returns no rows and nil['id'] is called before the category_id == 0 fallback can trigger

Migration inserts embeddable_hosts values verbatim including http:// schemes and paths, but the new exact host comparison in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host will reject referers for existing hosts entered with schemes/paths, silently breaking the feature after upgrade
Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy crash with 500 when the given ID doesn't exist because save_host(nil) and host.destroy are called on nil without a 404 check
Migration interpolates raw setting values into INSERT SQL without sanitization, allowing SQL injection or migration failure on values containing single quotes
The only tests for the new admin endpoints assert class inheritance, with no coverage of CRUD paths, category fallback, validation errors, or the EmbeddingSerializer/store hydration contract
The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb were accidentally swapped, putting each fabricator in the wrong file
Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing despite the route and frontend saveChanges action existing, so saving silently does nothing and returns unchanged data
No uniqueness constraint on the embeddable_hosts host column, allowing duplicate rows for the same host with different categories and nondeterministic category assignment in record_for_host

Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the :embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the old category fabricator definitions, likely an accidental file-swap/git mv mistake masked by global Fabricator registration

The update action in admin/embedding_controller.rb is a no-op dead implementation: fetch_embedding rebuilds the record from EmbeddableHost.all and nothing is ever written, yet routes, controller, serializer usage, and frontend JS save actions all exist to serve it

Migration's embed_category data conversion joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but the setting was consumed as a category id passed to PostCreator, so the join may silently fail leaving category_id == 0 and migrating all hosts to uncategorized

Migration irreversibly and unconditionally deletes legacy site settings ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') with no down path, even when the preceding conversion was skipped or produced a fallback category, making the original values unrecoverable

The removed SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard in topic.rb expandable_first_post? was replaced by nothing instead of an EmbeddableHost.exists? check, dropping the invariant that first-post truncation only applies while embedding is configured, and the related spec passes vacuously hiding the regression
Unrelated drive-by lint edits (unused variable removals) in topic_spec.rb digest specs have no connection to the embedding feature, polluting the diff and review surface
Locale key admin.embedding.edit is defined but never referenced by any template or component; the template uses icon-only buttons with no label, making it a dead locale entry
Admin embedding update action is a silent no-op: it re-renders the serializer without reading or persisting params, returning HTTP 200 while discarding the caller's payload

Host case normalization asymmetry: validation accepts uppercase hosts (regex with /i, no downcasing in before_validation) but record_for_host matches lower(host) = uri.host where URI host is always lowercase, so stored hosts like 'Eviltrout.com' can never match embed requests
No UNIQUE index on host (or lower(host)) in the embeddable_hosts migration, allowing the same host to be registered twice with .first arbitrarily picking one
Port is accepted by host validation regex but record_for_host compares against URI#host which excludes the port, making stored hosts with ports permanently unmatchable
Embeddable hosts controller update/destroy lack not-found guards, causing NoMethodError on nil (500) instead of 404 for stale or hand-crafted ids
category_id is assigned from params with no existence validation, no FK, and no presence check on the belongs_to :category association, allowing dead category references
Category deletion leaves embeddable_hosts rows dangling with no dependent/nullify hook, breaking TopicEmbed.import and causing embeds to fail or land in Uncategorized
category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have their contents swapped: the category file defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and the host file contains all the category fabricators
Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when 'embed_category' site setting was never set or doesn't match a category name, aborting db:migrate for default installs and blocking deploys

Migrated embeddable hosts are inserted raw via SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization that strips http(s):// prefixes and paths, causing previously allowed hosts to fail matching and get Discourse::InvalidAccess on /embed/comments
Migration permanently DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no rollback path, causing unrecoverable data loss if any INSERT fails midway or rollback is needed

Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains only the EmbeddableHost fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the Category fabricators, misleading future contributors editing the wrong file
embedding_controller.rb update action renders a serialization of the never-mutated @embedding, silently discarding all submitted changes from the PUT while responding 200 with success JSON
embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update and destroy fetch EmbeddableHost by id with no nil check, causing NoMethodError and HTTP 500 instead of a 404 or validation error for stale or fabricated ids
topic.rb expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, changing semantics so deleting all embeddable hosts no longer disables truncation for existing embedded topics
SQL string interpolation of unvalidated site setting values into raw INSERT in migration, allowing SQL injection or migration crash on single quotes
Unguarded nil on user-supplied params[:id] lookup in update and destroy actions of EmbeddableHostsController, causing unhandled 500 errors for stale or invalid ids

The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is only an ancestry assertion (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController), verifying none of the new behavior: the blank-category_id fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, the render_json_error path for invalid hosts, destroy of a nonexistent id (which would 500 on nil), or the serialization shape

Admin::EmbeddingController#update contains no persistence logic at all — it just re-renders the serialized @embedding — while the frontend saveChanges action calls update({}) expecting to save; no test issues a PUT and checks that anything changes, so the save embedding feature is a no-op that the passing suite gives false confidence about

The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test in topic_spec.rb now verifies a branch that no longer exists after removal of the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard from Topic#expandable_first_post?; it passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, and the new semantic (topic with has_topic_embed? and embed_truncate true is expandable even with zero hosts configured) has no coverage

The 'raises an error with a missing host' test in embed_controller_spec.rb is stale: it claims to cover host-config denial but passes only because no referer is stubbed, so the referer check fires instead; the new empty-hosts behavior (no rows in embeddable_hosts) is never directly asserted

The new plural _ids hydration branch in store.js.es6 is only tested on the happy path where all ids exist in the side-loaded payload; there is no test for an id absent from the root payload, where _lookupSubType returns null and the hydrated array silently contains null entries while the original _ids key is unconditionally deleted, crashing consumers like {{#each fruit.colors}} with unrecoverable data

The 'find embedded' test in store-test.js.es6 claims to load fruit 2 (banana, color_ids: [3]) but the pretender handler ignores the request id and always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids: [1,2]), so the assertions verify apple's data; the test passes only by mock accident and cannot catch hydration bugs specific to single-element color_ids arrays

The topic_embed.rb change replacing SiteSetting.embed_category with eh.try(:category_id) has only one spec assertion covering the matching-host case; no test exercises the branch where the imported URL's host is not registered (record_for_host returns nil), causing the topic to be created uncategorized instead of in the previously configured embed_category

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' setting row doesn't exist in site_settings or its value doesn't match a category name, because execute(...)[0] is nil on the default configuration
The 'uncategorized_category_id' fallback queries site_settings for a value that is a computed Ruby method on SiteSetting, not a database row, so the fallback path also crashes with NoMethodError

The migration irreversibly DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site_settings rows inside def change with no down method, backup, or restore path, permanently losing configuration on rollback

Migrated host values are inserted verbatim without normalizing schemes/paths, so hosts stored as 'http://discourse.org' never match the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host query comparing against uri.host, silently breaking previously-allowed embeds
Host values are interpolated into raw SQL INSERT statements without quoting or parameterization, allowing syntax errors or SQL injection from single quotes/backslashes in stored values

The deploy removes the settings from site_settings.yml and deletes SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? in the same step as the data migration, so old application servers during a rolling restart raise undefined-method/missing-setting errors with no expand/contract transitional phase

gold_ce_only: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

ce_bugs.t: Stored XSS: content imported with cook_method raw_html bypasses sanitization and is rendered raw in embed view and topic pages, allowing script execution from malicious feed content (nothing strips <script>, event handlers, or javascript: URLs; CGI.unescapeHTML even decodes entity-encoded markup)

Attribute injection: url in the 'imported from' footer in topic_embed.rb is not HTML-escaped, so a URL containing a single quote can break out of the href attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/elements

topic_embeds rows are never cleaned up when their topic/post is deleted, causing EmbedController#best to raise on stale topic_id (permanent 500 with no recovery path) and TopicEmbed.import update path to call PostRevisor.new(nil)

Remote fetches in import_remote (topic_embed.rb) and PollFeed use open-uri with no open_timeout/read_timeout and no response size limit, allowing slow or malicious hosts to hang Sidekiq workers and huge responses to exhaust memory

Every uncached embed/best hit enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no throttle at enqueue time, and each job synchronously runs a full feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute) over the network before falling back to the single-page fetch, enabling an unauthenticated attacker to flood the Sidekiq queue and multiply resource usage

The embed loading page (loading.html.erb) reloads every 30 seconds while the response is only cached for 1 minute, so every viewer of a pending embed keeps re-hitting the endpoint and re-enqueuing RetrieveTopic jobs, multiplying load by viewer count

Stored XSS via raw_html cook method: post.rb returns raw unsanitized HTML when cook_method is :raw_html, and embed/best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing script injection from third-party RSS feed content (which is only CGI.unescapeHTML'd, not sanitized) into the Discourse origin

RSS feed path (Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed -> TopicEmbed.import) passes raw feed content into raw_html cook path with no filtering, allowing script/iframe/onerror attributes in stored cooked content (stored XSS)
Even in the whitelisted path, the readability tag whitelist allows javascript: hrefs since attributes %w[href src] are permitted without scheme validation
topic_embed.rb:14 interpolates feed-controlled url directly into unescaped href='#{url}', allowing single-quote breakout into arbitrary HTML
force: true added to already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb, causing silent drop of the top_topics table and its data on any re-run
Disqus import CLI drops the --category method_option with no replacement, breaking existing callers passing -c
Rewriting Disqus import from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote silently discards created_at, so imported posts get import-time timestamps with no way to preserve the original
SimpleRSS.parse open(...) can raise on network/parse errors with no error handling in the poll feed job
Non-atomic setnx/expire throttle in TopicRetriever can leave a Redis key with no TTL if the process dies between calls, permanently blocking the embed URL for non-staff users
Anonymous /embed/best enqueues a RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job on every cache-miss for an unknown embed_url (user_id: nil), creating an unauthenticated job-enqueue/DoS vector

Stored XSS: remote HTML scraped via TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability tag whitelist doesn't sanitize attribute payloads like javascript: hrefs) is persisted and rendered raw with no sanitization on write or render path (Post#cook raw_html + embed view raw post.cooked)

HTML injection via embed_url in the 'imported from' footer in TopicEmbed.rb — url is interpolated directly into a single-quoted href with no escaping, allowing attribute breakout and stored XSS reachable from public /embed/best endpoint

No error handling or timeouts on any network fetch (PollFeed, import_remote open(url).read, TopicRetriever fetch_http) — network errors crash the poll with no log-and-continue, and the 60-second Redis throttle key is set before the fetch so transient failures with retry: false never actually retry

Infinite reload/retry loop with no terminal failure state — if retrieval permanently fails the loading page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely, each reload enqueues another RetrieveTopic job, and the throttle is bypassed entirely for staff (no_throttle: user.staff?) causing unbounded remote fetches

Referer-only guard with no rate limiting on the /embed/best enqueuing endpoint — forged Referer plus arbitrary embed_url enables request amplification against the job queue and embedded host; throttle is per-URL so varying the path bypasses it
Origin check in embed.js uses substring matching (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of exact origin parsing/comparison, breaking resize on scheme/port mismatches and misconfigured discourseUrl

Test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-48 asserts TopicRetriever is instantiated and retrieve is called, but EmbedController#best enqueues a background job and never instantiates TopicRetriever directly, so the expectation cannot be satisfied by the real code (test verifies mocks, not the job enqueue/argument passing/fallback render behavior)

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2 has a copy-paste error: require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post' instead of the poll feed job, documenting the wrong dependency; similarly topic_retriever_spec.rb requires 'topic_retriever' as a dependency while retrieve_topic.rb relies on auto-requiring it
Raw-HTML cook path returns unsanitized external content as cooked HTML, which embed/best.html.erb renders with raw post.cooked, enabling XSS from the embedded host's content
TopicRetriever#fetch_http crashes with NoMethodError on nil when SiteSetting.embed_by_username is blank but embeddable_host is set (lib/topic_retriever.rb:47)

PollFeed and the retriever re-evaluate guard conditions inconsistently (PollFeed checks feed_polling_url/embed_by_username, the retriever doesn't), and the two entry points can race on TopicEmbed.import
Unescaped URL interpolated into single-quoted HTML attribute in the imported-from footer (app/models/topic_embed.rb:14), allowing attribute breakout since URL is only validated by /^https?::////

Check-then-create race on topic_embeds.embed_url unique index in TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:19-31): concurrent workers race and the loser raises on the unique index with no rescue, and PollFeed sets retry: false so the failure is silent

Modified already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adds force: true, which drops and recreates the top_topics table in environments where the migration hasn't run, silently discarding data
String#scrub in poll_feed.rb:38 requires Ruby 2.1+, an implicit runtime constraint not declared anywhere
Duplicated embed-user lookup (User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first) in poll_feed.rb:27 and topic_retriever.rb:47 with divergent nil-guarding

`force: true` on `create_table :topic_embeds` will silently drop an existing topic_embeds table before recreating it, destroying embed→topic mappings and content_sha1 bookkeeping with no rollback or warning

`force: true` added to already-committed migration CreateTopTopics is destructive DDL that drops the top_topics table and all its aggregated ranking data if the migration re-runs while the table exists

Raw HTML import path (Post.rb cook_method raw_html combined with embed/best.html.erb rendering raw post.cooked) bypasses the sanitizer and after_post_cook filters, resulting in stored XSS on the Discourse origin for embed visitors
topic_embeds lacks index/FK on topic_id and post_id, so deleted topics leave orphaned embed rows that cause EmbedController#best to raise on a missing topic instead of gracefully falling back

embed_url is stored and compared without normalization, so scheme/trailing-slash variants create duplicate topics for the same article and cause lookups to miss existing embeds and re-enqueue retrieval forever
The raw_html cook method in post.rb:131 bypasses the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline with no downstream sanitization

PollFeed passes unescaped feed content (i.content) straight to TopicEmbed.import with no tag/attribute whitelist, allowing script, iframe, onerror handlers, or javascript: hrefs to be stored and rendered verbatim
embed/best.html.erb renders post.cooked with raw output, so stored malicious HTML from feeds is rendered unsanitized

The readability path (import_remote) whitelists a[href] but does not sanitize URL schemes, so javascript: hrefs survive; absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs starting with / and does not sanitize schemes
/embed/best is served from the forum's own origin with X-Frame-Options set to ALLOWALL, so injected scripts execute with full access on the forum origin

mrv_bugs: poll_feed.rb: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no error handling, so one network failure or 500 response on the feed URL permanently kills the feed polling job
topic_retriever.rb:50: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence check, crashing with NoMethodError on nil when embed_by_username is blank but embeddable_host is set

topic_embed.rb:24-31: TopicEmbed is not destroyed when its topic or post is deleted (no dependent: :destroy), causing EmbedController#best to raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound and return a permanent 500 for that embed URL
topic_embed.rb: update path does PostRevisor.new(embed.post) with a nil post after post deletion, causing NoMethodError inside the hourly PollFeed job

create_top_topics.rb migration: changing an already-committed migration to use force: true silently drops the existing top_topics table in environments where the table exists but the migration hasn't run, causing data loss

topic_embed.rb:60-77: absolutize_urls only handles leading-slash URLs, so protocol-relative (//cdn.example.com/...) and bare-relative (images/foo.jpg) URLs pass through unchanged and render broken inside the embedded topic
topic_embed.rb:23-29: when content_sha1 changes, only the post body is revised — the topic title is never updated, leaving stale titles on edited articles

topic_embed.rb:15-21: unique index race on TopicEmbed.create! — concurrent imports of the same URL (controller path vs PollFeed) raise unrescued ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, crashing the job and rolling back the topic

Unrelated rewrite of the Disqus import task in lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-141 removes the --category CLI option and drops created_at, causing imported Disqus topics to lose category targeting and be stamped with import time instead of the original thread date
External untrusted HTML from feed content is stored and rendered as raw cooked content with no sanitization, enabling arbitrary script execution from a compromised feed (XSS)
Even the readability path whitelists tags but keeps href/src attributes verbatim, so javascript: URLs in links survive sanitization
The 30-second reload loop in loading.html.erb has no terminal state, backoff, or client-side stop condition, so a URL that can never be imported reloads and re-enqueues forever

No URL normalization on the embed_url join key between the two ingestion paths (feed link vs discourseEmbedUrl), so discrepancies like trailing slashes, http vs https, or query strings cause permanent lookup misses and duplicate topic imports

No dependent: :destroy, FK, or destroy hook for TopicEmbed rows, so deleting the imported post or topic leaves a dangling TopicEmbed; the next feed poll then crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! with NoMethodError
Disqus import via TopicEmbed.import_remote silently loses created_at, giving every imported thread the current timestamp and destroying chronological ordering of the archive

Outbound fetches in TopicRetriever and TopicEmbed use bare open-uri with no explicit timeout, so a slow remote site stalls the RetrieveTopic worker indefinitely and locks out retries for that URL for 60s

Unsanitized URL interpolated into raw HTML footer in app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 allows stored XSS; the ^https?:// regex validation passes malicious URLs like http://x.com/"><script>alert(1)</script>, which are rendered raw via cook_method: raw_html
The sanitization intent of import_remote (readability tag whitelist) is silently undone by the import method appending the unescaped URL fragment in the same code path

RSS content path in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 has no sanitization at all; PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import directly bypassing the readability whitelist, so arbitrary HTML including <script> and <iframe> is stored verbatim as cooked and rendered raw, enabling stored XSS from a malicious feed
A single malformed feed item permanently blocks the entire feed import: i.content is nil on RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide description, causing NoMethodError on nil.scrub that aborts the loop

No per-item rescue in PollFeed combined with sidekiq_options retry: false means one bad item or open() failure prevents all subsequent items from being imported and the job fails silently with no retry every hour forever

Disqus import in lib/tasks/disqus.thor silently changed behavior: --category option and original timestamps dropped; new behavior scrapes remote article body, uses current timestamps, and cannot target a category

No failure path in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 with loading view; if retrieval fails no TopicEmbed row is created, so every subsequent request re-enqueues and re-renders 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely
Loading view's 30-second setTimeout reload combined with 1-minute response caching means even on success visitors can stare at a reloading 'Loading' screen for up to a minute

Update path in app/models/topic_embed.rb:31 crashes on orphaned embeds; posts can be deleted by moderators while topic_embeds row remains, so embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises, killing the whole scheduled poll

Unrelated modification of already-shipped migration db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb: force: true will silently DROP TABLE any existing top_topics data if run against a database where the table exists outside schema-migrations; appears to be a local-dev hack

The PR folds in three unacknowledged objective changes (raw_html trust model, Disqus tool rewrite, unrelated migration modifications) beyond its stated 'embed URL handling and validation' objective; items #1, #2, #4 combined constitute a security regression that should block merge until the footer is escaped and both import paths run through a common sanitizer

Stored XSS: Post#cook returns raw content when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing the sanitization pipeline; TopicEmbed.import stores un-sanitized external HTML as post.cooked which is rendered with raw post.cooked in the embed view (app/models/post.rb:131, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:21)

PollFeed imports feed content with zero HTML filtering: raw RSS content is passed directly to TopicEmbed.import which stores it as raw_html; CGI.unescapeHTML actively decodes entities, re-materializing encoded script tags as live markup (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-33)

Unescaped URL interpolated into a single-quoted href attribute in the imported_from footer with no escaping; the upstream validation regex permits quotes and spaces, enabling attribute-injection stored XSS from feed item links (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8)

SSRF via redirect-following defeats the host check: open-uri transparently follows HTTP redirects so an open redirect on the embeddable host lets the server-side fetch pivot to internal services like cloud metadata endpoints; the invalid_host? check never re-runs on redirects (app/models/topic_embed.rb:41-42, lib/topic_retriever.rb:15-17)

Referer header used as an authorization gate: Referer is fully client-controlled so any non-browser client can forge it to bypass the embeddable_host check, while also denying legitimate users whose privacy extensions strip Referer (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-28)
Migrations use force: true in create_table, which drops pre-existing tables and risks data loss (db/migrate/20131217233733_create_topic_embeds.rb, 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb)
Orphaned topic_embeds rows cause EmbedController#best to 500 on the publisher's page by calling TopicView.new on a dead topic_id

Orphaned topic_embeds rows permanently poison the embed URL: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve bails on TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?, the unique index blocks re-import, and TopicEmbed.import takes the update branch and crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil) since embed.post is nil

topic_embed.rb:29 unconditionally persists the new content_sha1 via update_column even when the PostRevisor revise! failed or returned false, so future polls skip the revision and source article changes are never synced to the post with no error surfaced

poll_feed.rb: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no error handling, so one network failure or 500 response on the feed URL permanently kills the feed polling job

topic_embed.rb: update path does PostRevisor.new(embed.post) with a nil post after post deletion, causing NoMethodError inside the hourly PollFeed job

embed_controller_spec.rb:48-53: the success rendering path mocks TopicView, so best.html.erb (including nil user and blank posts branches) has never been executed by any test

Modification of existing applied migration db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adds force: true, which drops the existing top_topics table and destroys all its rows if the migration is ever re-run
embed.js in app/assets/javascripts/ is never servable or distributed: the diff contains no route, precompile-list addition, or documented include path, making the embed feature unusable as shipped
Dead code in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22: feed_key is defined but never referenced, pointing maintainers at a caching invariant that does not exist

Dead client locale entry in config/locales/client.en.yml:1477 adds 'embedding' to the client-side admin settings category list but no corresponding site settings have client: true, leaving an unrenderable UI string
Unrelated whitespace churn in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb (trailing-whitespace fixup and removal of trailing newline) pollutes the history of an unrelated pre-existing migration

Even the readability path whitelists tags but keeps href/src attributes verbatim, so javascript: URLs in links survive sanitization

feed_key is computed in PollFeed but never used; the feed-modified check to skip re-parsing unchanged feeds is unimplemented dead code, causing unbounded re-fetching and re-parsing proportional to feed size on a hot path

i.content.scrub in PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on standard RSS 2.0 feeds because SimpleRSS leaves content nil for description-based items, and with retry: false the polling job dies silently so no topics are ever imported via polling

TopicRetriever synchronously re-runs the entire feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) inline to service a single URL retrieval, doing O(whole feed) work per request with the throttle bypassed for staff users

The 30-second reload loop in loading.html.erb has no terminal state, backoff, or client-side stop condition, so a URL that can never be imported reloads and re-enqueues forever

ce_bugs.t: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members: the server hard-caps at limit 50 and the public members route fetches once with no pagination UI in members.hbs, so end users can never see more than 50 members

The usernames input is not cleared after addMembers, so a second click of 'Add' re-submits the same users

Unbounded client-controlled limit and offset on the public group members endpoint: limit is not clamped to a maximum and offset is not clamped to >= 0, allowing clients to defeat pagination and trigger unbounded queries/materialization (and a negative offset causes a 500)
No bound on the size of the usernames payload in add_members, allowing a single request to carry tens of thousands of usernames and making the N+1 cost unbounded

findMembers clamps offset using possibly-stale user_count before the request, causing wrong computed offsets in findMembers and admin-group next/previous actions, leading to wasted duplicate fetches and wrong-page UX

Breaking response-shape change on public GET /groups/:group_id/members: previously returned a bare serialized array, now returns { members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }, breaking external consumers that map over the array, with no versioning or deprecation path

Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls added to the members template (unlike the admin template which got next/previous actions), a functional regression for large groups

Admin API contract break: create and update in admin/groups_controller.rb now read flat params (params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]) instead of nested group[...] params, breaking external API consumers that POST {group: {name: ...}}

Removed PATCH membership API (update_patch handling params[:changes][:add]/[:delete]) and PUT group[usernames] full-replacement logic, but PATCH and PUT still route to update and return success_json while silently no-oping membership changes

Pagination off-by-one in totalPages computed in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts when user_count is a multiple of limit, causing navigation to an empty page and showLast never being true on the real last page so the next arrow is never disabled
After removing the last member of a page, the stale offset is not backed up to the previous page, causing findMembers to return an empty member list
remove_member can raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound (unhandled 500) when the user_id is not currently a member, due to has_many :through delete with no pre-check
Public members endpoint accepts unbounded limit (e.g. limit=1000000) that can serialize the entire user table, and unvalidated values allow arbitrary limits on public endpoints
Public members endpoint accepts unvalidated negative offset which produces invalid SQL on Postgres, causing a 500

No guard against concurrent/out-of-order member fetches: pagination buttons aren't disabled while fetching and there's no request sequencing, so rapid clicks can leave displayed list and pagination state inconsistent
Controller specs call actions directly with hand-fed group_id, bypassing routing and masking the route param-name mismatch; a request or routing spec would have caught it
New frontend pagination logic untested and totalPages = floor(user_count / limit) + 1 has an off-by-one producing an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit

Pagination math is computed in three places with three sources of truth (controller computeds, controller next/previous actions, model findMembers re-clamping, plus server meta), allowing them to disagree

totalPages off-by-one: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 returns an extra page when user_count is exactly divisible by limit (100 users / 50 per page shows 3 pages and 'next' navigates to an empty page); should be Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1
findMembers has an inconsistent return contract: returns undefined when group name is empty but a Promise otherwise, breaking any caller that chains .then()
findMembers addresses the group by mutable user-editable name instead of id, causing 404s or wrong-group fetches after a rename

Duplicated fire-and-forget member loading (model.findMembers() with no rejection handling) in both admin_group_route setupController and group-members route, swallowing failures and leaving the UI silently empty on network errors
Spec 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses xhr :put, remove_member but the route is delete, so the test doesn't actually exercise remove_member; it should use xhr :delete

Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls — limit is unconditionally applied server-side and the public group/members.hbs template has no next/previous UI, hiding members from end users

totalPages computed property in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count/limit) + 1, producing an off-by-one phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil

group_member.hbs remove link guards on `automatic` but the item template's context is the member (Discourse.User) which has no automatic property, so the guard evaluates falsy and the remove icon is shown on automatic groups, yielding 422 errors when clicked

remove_member executes group.users.delete(user_id) immediately (destroying the join row) before group.save, so if group.save fails afterward the controller reports an error even though the member was already removed, leaving stale UI
remove_member spec uses xhr :put for a DELETE-routed action, exercising the action with the wrong HTTP verb because controller specs bypass routing, hiding the P1 param mismatch

Stale-count race in pagination: next/findMembers clamp offsets against locally cached user_count with no request-sequencing guard, allowing offset == user_count and a permanently empty last page under concurrent mutations or out-of-order promise resolution
