ce_bugs.t: Dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent: the .find() predicate compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId but only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar is always undefined, causing google.events.update with calendarId: undefined and silent failure of reschedules/edits for legacy bookings
Same dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent leads to calendarId: undefined when cancelling legacy bookings, resulting in orphaned Google calendar events after cancellation

Duplicate event creation when multiple destinations lack credentialId: each destination without credentialId fans out to all matching calendarCredentials, creating the event N times for N destinations

BaseCalendarService.createEvent filter pins to first host's calendar externalId, so when called with host B's credential the filter compares against host A's externalId, creating zero events for non-first hosts' calendars in multi-host collective bookings

Team destination calendars silently dropped when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar: evt.destinationCalendar is null and the optional-chained ?.push() skips adding teamDestinationCalendars
Only destinationCalendar[0] is persisted on the Booking, so hosts 2..N lose their destination context in reschedule/cancel/email flows that reconstruct from booking.destinationCalendar
Google organizer email pinned to first host's destination externalId on every host's calendar in createEvent and updateEvent, misattributing events on non-first hosts' calendars
Recurring bulk-delete now executes once per calendar reference inside the bookingCalendarReference loop instead of once, causing duplicate delete API calls, error noise, and potential rate-limiting

Google updateEvent fallback predicate searches for externalId === externalCalendarId in a branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the fallback never matches and calendarId becomes undefined, breaking reschedules of legacy bookings without externalCalendarId (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~253)

Google deleteEvent has the same broken fallback: when externalCalendarId is absent, calendarId is undefined instead of the destination calendar's external ID, leaving orphaned Google events when cancelling legacy bookings (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~312-315)

getUsersCredentials uses the caller's rather than the organizer's credentials for eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, likely causing failure or no-op for non-organizer callers

isTeamAdminOrOwner permission check uses && , requiring the user to be both admin and owner simultaneously, which is suspicious and likely should be || , potentially blocking legitimate admins or owners from adding guests

Non-atomic multi-step write in addGuests.handler.ts (~105-126): the createMany commits before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails run, so a failure in those steps leaves attendee rows permanently in the DB with no calendar update or emails, and retry becomes impossible because uniqueGuests filters out already-added guests and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, leaving a half-migrated state with no repair path
getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) is called even when ctx.user is only an attendee, so an attendee-triggered add uses the attendee's credentials which frequently have no calendar integration

TOCTOU race on the duplicate filter in addGuests.handler.ts (~85-90): dedup is done in application code against a booking snapshot with no unique constraint or upsert, so concurrent addGuests calls (e.g. double-clicking Add) both pass the filter and create duplicate (bookingId, email) rows that propagate to calendar and email lists with no cleanup path

Silent partial application of guests: the filter silently removes already-existing emails (e.g. existing@y.com) and the mutation returns 'Guests added', giving the user no way to know only a subset was applied; the result should report added vs skipped

Notification failure swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts (~170-174): sendAddGuestsEmails errors are reduced to a console.log that drops the error object, the handler still returns success, and there is no retry, dead-letter record, or 'added but never notified' state marking

Missing seat capacity enforcement in addGuests.handler.ts (~65-68): the handler reads booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot but never enforces it before createMany, creating plain Attendee rows on the parent booking that overbook past the seat limit and are disconnected from seat tracking (seatReferenceUid), violating a data invariant other code paths rely on

gold_ce_only: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

gold_ce_only: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
gold_mrv_only: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

gold_ce_only: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

ce_bugs.t: Webhook endpoint findFirst-then-create/update is not atomic; concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate credentials for the same userId/appId

Webhook secret comparison fails open if both header and configured secret are undefined, is not timing-safe, and uppercase characters in CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME cause all requests to 403 since Node lowercases header names

minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed zod keys evaluate to a duplicate literal ('[object Object]') rather than a dynamic-key matcher, so the intended 'any property with a number is the expiry' behavior never exists
Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so in sync mode the parsed result is essentially {access_token} only, dropping expiry_date/expires_in fields

The fallback refresh_token = 'refresh_token' overwrites the real refresh token when merged/persisted (e.g. office365's spread of tokenResponse.data), permanently breaking token refresh for those credentials
zoho-bigin and zohocrm consume the fetch Response as an axios shape (tokenInfo.data), causing undefined access and a throw on !tokenInfo.data.error
Hubspot uses the raw fetch Response as HubspotToken, persisting garbage/undefined into credential.key
No response.ok/status validation is performed on the sync endpoint's response before it is persisted as a credential

zoho-bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, sending the wrong calcomUserId to the sync endpoint and causing cross-user credential mixing/IDOR-style credential misrouting
Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText !== 'OK', which fails spuriously for HTTP/2 or non-200 2xx responses with empty/non-'OK' statusText

Webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual), permitting a potential timing side channel on an endpoint that can create/overwrite any user's app credentials
Webhook handler throws unhandled 500s (instead of returning 400) on malformed request bodies from schema.parse and on bad ciphertext/JSON from symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse
Decrypted keys are persisted as credential.key with no validation against the app's credential schema, allowing arbitrary JSON values to corrupt credential rows

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` result is stored as the whole SafeParseReturnType wrapper in `credential.key`, so downstream code finds `access_token`/`expiry_date` undefined and every calendar operation re-enters `refreshAccessToken`, causing extra network round trips and DB writes (affects googlecalendar, office365calendar, and zoomvideo)

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` computed keys via `[z.string().toString()]` degenerate into the same literal key (second overwrites first), and without `.passthrough()` the parsed data strips all fields except `access_token`, dropping expiry info so expiry-based refresh gating never works in sync mode and causing a refresh (network + DB write) on every operation

Webhook `app-credential.ts` accepts `keys: z.string()` with no `max()` bound and writes the decrypted blob directly to `Credential.key`, allowing arbitrarily large payloads to be loaded into memory on every calendar operation
Google Calendar credential key persisted as SafeParseReturn wrapper instead of parsed token payload, corrupting stored credential shape for all users on next token refresh (CalendarService.ts:96)

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses z.string().toString() which evaluates to literal '[object Object]' keys, effectively reducing schema to { access_token } and silently stripping expiry_date/expires_in and other fields (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-9)
Hubspot call site treats refreshOAuthTokens result as parsed HubspotToken object; in sync mode it's a fetch Response whose body is never read (CalendarService.ts:177)
Zoho and Zoho-Bigin call sites access .data on the refresh result; a fetch Response has no .data and the body is never consumed (zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:85, zohocrm CalendarService.ts:204)
Google Calendar call site dereferences res?.data then token.access_token; in sync mode res is a fetch Response with no .data, throwing on undefined dereference (CalendarService.ts:86-92)

Office365 calendar refresh contract changed from graceful degradation (log and continue with stale credentials on safeParse failure) to throwing an error on schema mismatch, and error logging was removed (CalendarService.ts:261-265)

Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok/status; statusText is empty for HTTP/2 responses in undici fetch, so successful refreshes over HTTP/2 would throw HttpError 400, and non-2xx errors surface as confusing zod failures (CalendarService.ts:88)

parseRefreshTokenResponse writes placeholder refresh_token: 'refresh_token' into credential data, so if sync is later disabled the stored credential contains a literal garbage refresh token sent to providers by the non-sync refresh path

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of parsed data, and Google CalendarService writes it directly to prisma.credential.update, corrupting every Google credential's stored key after first token refresh

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `z.string().toString()` as a dynamic key, which evaluates to the static key "[object Object]" (both properties collide and overwrite), so the schema strips expiry/refresh fields from refreshed tokens
`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response but HubSpot CalendarService casts it as HubspotToken, so refresh_token/access_token reads yield undefined in sync mode
Zoho Bigin CalendarService reads `tokenInfo.data.error` off a fetch Response which has no `.data` property, throwing TypeError on every refresh in sync mode
ZohoCRM CalendarService reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`/`.expiryDate` off a fetch Response, throwing TypeError on every refresh in sync mode

Salesforce CalendarService uses `response.statusText !== "OK"` as success check, which fails on HTTP/2 where undici returns an empty statusText, causing successful 200 responses to throw HttpError 400; should use response.ok

App credential webhook handler calls `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` without error handling, so undecryptable or invalid-JSON keys throw and produce 500s rather than clean 400s, with no logging to distinguish bad payloads from internal errors
Office365 refresh behavior change: previously a schema mismatch degraded gracefully by keeping old credentials; now it throws and fails the entire calendar operation

Google Calendar CalendarService stores the full SafeParseReturnType object from parseRefreshTokenResponse instead of .data, persisting {success, data, error} as the credential key and permanently destroying the stored Google refresh token (access_token/refresh_token become undefined on next read)

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but an AxiosResponse (or refreshFunction result) in normal mode, with no unified return contract; zoho-bigin, zohocrm, and hubspot callers access .data or cast to HubspotToken, which silently breaks with undefined fields when credential sharing/sync mode is enabled

Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses z.string().toString() as a computed key, which evaluates to '[object Object]' instead of a wildcard key; the duplicate keys cause the z.number() expiry validation to be silently dropped — .passthrough() or .catchall() should be used instead
parseRefreshTokenResponse injects a refresh_token = 'refresh_token' sentinel placeholder literal that gets persisted into real credential rows, which is confusing and fragile
Webhook app-credential endpoint compares the secret with !== (not timing-safe) instead of a constant-time comparison like crypto.timingSafeEqual

Webhook app-credential endpoint reads req.headers[name] which is typed string | string[] | undefined, so a repeated header yields an array and the secret comparison always fails with confusing 403s; also a non-lowercase env value would silently miss in the headers lookup

Webhook app-credential route handler lets ZodError from body schema parse and SyntaxError from JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt propagate as unhandled 500s with stack traces instead of mapped 400/422 responses

.env.example gives contradictory key-size instructions: says the key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but instructs 'openssl rand -base64 24' (24 bytes), which can break symmetricDecrypt for self-hosters following the example
Google Calendar persists the zod parse-result wrapper as the credential key instead of parsed data, corrupting credentials on every token refresh and permanently breaking the integration

Sync-mode response contract mismatch: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect app-specific shapes (googlecalendar, hubspot, larkcalendar, zoho), breaking the credential sharing path
zoho-bigin passes credentialId as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint instead of credential.userId, provisioning credentials for the wrong principal
minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys evaluate to literal '[object Object]' string keys, making the dynamic-key expiry validation a no-op and silently dropping expiry fields in sync mode
Fake refresh_token = 'refresh_token' placeholder is persisted to the database, overwriting and irreversibly destroying real refresh tokens
Salesforce performs an unconditional token refresh and DB write on every service construction even when the access token is valid, adding latency and turning transient outages into thrown errors
Outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication/secret header and never checks the response status, allowing unverified callers and cascading parse failures
Webhook secret comparison uses !== (not constant-time) and mis-compares array-valued headers; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual
Webhook body schema parse throws a raw ZodError, resulting in an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 response

mrv_bugs: Unknown properties in the token response are stripped by zod rather than passed through, so expiry fields are silently dropped from every refreshed token persisted to credential.key

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-7 - z.string().toString() evaluates to literal '[object String]', so both computed keys are identical constants and the second overwrites the first; combined with z.object's strip behavior the schema only validates access_token and strips expiry_date, so token responses with no expiry pass validation and callers store undefined expiry_date

gold_mrv_only: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

ce_bugs.t: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync endpoint returns a fetch Response but this caller reads the provider client's res.data shape, so parent-supplied tokens are never parsed and Google refreshes fail.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — The new helper returns a Zod SafeParse result rather than credential data, and this stores { success, data } as the Google credential so later consumers cannot read access_token or expiry_date.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod SafeParse wrapper (`{success,data}`), and it is persisted as-is via `data: { key }`, so the stored credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` and the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails for every refreshed Google credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal "[object Object]", so `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is effectively `{access_token: string}` with all other keys (expiry, refresh_token, instance_url, etc.) stripped in credential-sync mode; the intended "any numeric property is expiry" rule never applies.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60 — If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the header is absent, `undefined !== undefined` is false and the secret check passes; the handler relies entirely on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (defined outside this diff) to gate that case.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:97 — findFirst` on `{userId, appId}` picks an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app (e.g. multiple Google accounts) and overwrites it; the update also never resets `invalid: false`, so a credential previously marked invalid stays invalid after fresh keys are synced.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys evaluate to literal property names rather than wildcards, so the shared sync schema silently stops enforcing its stated expiry-field contract and future integrations will rely on a misleading boundary.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — This shared parser takes `any` and `ZodTypeAny`, so replacing provider schemas with the sync schema erases the credential shape at the OAuth boundary and lets incompatible persisted keys compile.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every SalesforceCalendarService construction refreshes and persists the token, adding a remote call and database write to each Salesforce calendar operation.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync path returns a raw Fetch Response although Google and HubSpot read provider token fields directly, so expired shared credentials fail to refresh and retry on each use.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The new parent credential-sync request has no timeout, so a stalled parent application can hold calendar and video refresh requests until runtime timeout.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Shared-secret comparison uses `!==` rather than crypto.timingSafeEqual, making it timing-sensitive.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret header/signature) and the parent app returns live access tokens for any calcomUserId, so the sync endpoint must be unauthenticated or rely on network trust; the response is also trusted unvalidated.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — Decrypted payload is JSON.parse'd and written verbatim to credential.key with no per-app schema validation; symmetricDecrypt is called with "" when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, and both failures surface as unhandled 500s.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The credential-sync validation branch has no test with a normal token payload, so the computed "[object Object]" required key can reject every refresh response and break token renewal.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — The new webhook has no authentication test for an unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, so requests with no header are accepted and can create or replace credentials.
